newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian police fire teargas to disperse Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian police fire teargas to disperse Moslems.

text.p: Police in the northern Nigeria city of Kaduna on Wednesday fired teargas to disperse Shi'ite Moslems demonstrating against the arrest of their leaders, witnesses said.
They said more than 1,000 protesters were dispersed when the Moslems took to the streets for the second time in as many weeks over the detention of their leaders.
"Anti-riot police men were out in full force to stop the demonstration," said a journalist from Kaduna, adding that he was not aware of any casualties.
There was no immediate comment from the police in Kaduna.
Police in the mainly Moslem north, scene of bloody religious riots in the past, have been placed on alert over an ultimatum given by a Shi'ite Moslem group after the arrest of its firebrand leader.

At a news conference in Kaduna, Police Commissioner Yakubu Shaibu urged the public to disregard the ultimatum which said there would be trouble if the group's leader Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky and others were not released by Wednesday and warned they would deal firmly with any breach of the peace.
On Saturday the Shi'ites' Moslem Brotherhood said 14 people had been killed in clashes with police at the weekend following El-Zak-Zaky's arrest. Police deny there were deaths.
Last month three people were killed in a clash between rival sects in Kano, the region's biggest city.
Moslems, predominantly Sunni, make up roughly half of Nigeria's 100 million people.
